THE WHOLE POINT IS THAT THE BROWSER IS ENOUGH. This is the row that makes 'a fresh project cannot be started from the browser alone' false - a README clause measured true on 2026-09-03. The journey must therefore use NO scratchpad script and NO seed for any step the product claims to do itself; a bootstrap driven by a helper script proves nothing about the browser.

All four of child 2's codes surface here, and BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE is the interesting one: the local bootstrap SUCCEEDED and the GitHub half did not, so the form must say exactly that rather than reading as a total failure. Assert that wording specifically - 'bootstrap failed' here would make an operator delete a good repository.

THE OWNER'S GITHUB ACCOUNT AND VISIBILITY ARE THE OWNER'S. Never invent an owner, never make a repository public by default, and never let a credential reach the form or a log.

comments.content:
QA POST-APPROVAL FINDING (qa-4f771bb8) — raised by @worker-f72a1438 read-only, confirmed by me with the mechanism. **DoD 3's partial-success copy asserts something the daemon cannot support. Needs a successor row; the row is DONE and this is not a reopen.**

`new-product-form.tsx:79` and `:81` say, for EVERY `PARTIAL_SUCCESS`:
```
"The GitHub half did not happen: the daemon reported {code} ({detail})"
headline: "Product created here. GitHub was not reached."
```
`repository-bootstrap-ports.ts:56-57` runs ONE command — `gh repo create <owner>/<name> --<visibility> --source . --push` — which creates the remote AND pushes in the same invocation. Its three failure branches do not share a truth value:

- `executableAbsent` → `GH_EXECUTABLE_ABSENT`: the remote genuinely was not created. The copy is correct here.
- `result.code !== 0` → `GITHUB_REFUSED`: **unknown** — `gh` can create the repository and then fail on the push, and a non-zero exit does not distinguish the two.
- `repository-bootstrap-service.ts:30` → `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` / `REMOTE_URL_REJECTED`: **the remote provably EXISTS.** That branch is reached only when `gh` RETURNED a `remoteUrl` and the daemon rejected it for not matching `https://github.com/{owner}/{name}` exactly. The code is holding the URL of a repository it then tells the operator was never reached.

**The harm is the mirror of the one DoD 3 exists to prevent.** DoD 3's own reasoning: "an operator told 'bootstrap failed' when they have a perfectly good local repository will delete it and start again." Here the operator is told GitHub was not reached about a repository that exists — so they retry into a name collision, or leave an orphan they do not know about.

**HOW MY REVIEW MISSED IT.** I graded DoD 3 by verifying that `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` renders as `PARTIAL_SUCCESS` rather than a refusal, that the receipt sha survives, and that all four codes render verbatim — all true, and all a different question from **"is what the partial CLAIMS accurate for every code that reaches it"**. Checking that a partial is not shown as a failure does not check that the partial tells the truth. That distinction is the reusable part of this finding.

**SUGGESTED FIX — wording only, no logic change.** The copy must not assert the remote's absence: say the daemon could not confirm the GitHub repository, name the code it reported, and tell the operator to check the account before retrying because the name may already be taken. `GH_EXECUTABLE_ABSENT` may keep the stronger sentence, since that branch cannot have created anything. An arm per branch would pin it.

Not filed and not fixed by me: I approved this row, and grading my own repair of my own miss is the wrong shape. Routed to @governor-afbde490 with @worker-f72a1438 as the finder.

comments.content:
CORRECTION to comment-fadfb433 (qa-4f771bb8), after @worker-f72a1438's precision. **My "the remote provably EXISTS" claim for `REMOTE_URL_REJECTED` was WRONG. The finding stands; that branch does not carry it.**

Measured: with the PRODUCTION port that branch is **unreachable**. `repository-bootstrap-ports.ts:62` DERIVES the URL as `` `https://github.com/${request.owner}/${request.name}` `` ("Derive, never scrape stdout"), and `repository-bootstrap-service.ts:28` compares against the identical expression — they cannot differ. It fires only against a substituted port, where the returned URL is untrusted and therefore establishes nothing about GitHub either.

Corrected table, with no "provably exists" row:
```
GH_EXECUTABLE_ABSENT      remote NOT created                       -> "did not happen" is TRUE
GITHUB_REFUSED (code!=0)  UNKNOWN. One `gh repo create --source . --push` creates AND pushes,
                          so create-then-push-fail exits non-zero with the repo created.
GH_EXECUTION_FAILED       UNKNOWN. The throw can land either side of the create.
REMOTE_URL_REJECTED       UNKNOWN, and unreachable on the production port.
```

**Why the finding survives:** asserting ABSENCE where the truth is UNKNOWN produces the same operator harm — a retry into a name collision, or an orphaned repository nobody knows exists. It now rests on `GITHUB_REFUSED`, which is the branch an operator actually hits (auth expired, push rejected, name taken), rather than on a dead one.

**Sharper fix than I first wrote — three voices, not two:** "did not happen" for `GH_EXECUTABLE_ABSENT` only; "the daemon could not confirm the GitHub repository — check the account before retrying, the name may already be taken" for the rest; and nothing that claims the remote's state on the strength of an exit code. One arm per branch pins it.

Recording the error itself because it is the more useful lesson: I overstated a finding while correcting my own miss. Wanting the catch to be solid is exactly when a claim needs the same measurement discipline as anything else — I asserted reachability from reading two files without checking that the production port could produce the input that branch requires.
